title: Withdraw a pending invitation safely from exceptions

outcomes.statement: An authorized Group Admin withdraws exactly the selected pending invitation with a required note, releases its seat reservation only after provider success, and sees the durable withdrawn action in the request trail.
outcomes.demo: Withdraw an overdue invitation from exceptions and verify the provider invitation deletion, invited-to-deprovisioned transition, freed reservation and note in Acciones; race with acceptance and prove no active member or assignment is removed.

uncertainties.statement: Generic deprovision is unsafe for invitation hygiene.
uncertainties.resolution: packages/connectors/src/providers/anthropic/connector.ts deprovision enumerates members and invitations by email and may call delete_member. DEC-SMP-023 and child AC1/AC2 require a distinct vendor-neutral invitation-only operation pinned to provisioning_action.vendor_ref. Reuse provider transport and observation with Pact-backed delete_invite, shared request/action locking, acceptance-race refusal and fail-closed ambiguous outcomes; release reservation only after confirmed deletion. The original manual-invite-withdrawal proposal budgets 35 minutes for this boundary within its 310-minute total. Official provider contract https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management (Members and invites; Withdraw an invite) permits only pending invitations and returns 400 for accepted/expired invitations. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/invites/delete returns 200 with matching id and type invite_deleted. Validate both, reject all missing/malformed/ambiguous confirmation; never remove a member. Use a committed withdraw_invite intent and original invitation advisory lock across I/O; keep rows unlocked during observation persistence, recheck under row locks at finalization. Durable matching successful deletion receipt permits finalize-only recovery; requested-only evidence refuses blind retries. This is one invitation withdrawal lifecycle/concurrency boundary.
